source_attention_item_reason: Decider self-applied EXP-640.c1 minor_edit: §7.4 TLDR firmament height changed from (8,500 km) to (8,537 km at the pole). Verify the §7.3 TLDR (which still says 8,500 km as a general bound) remains accurate and consistent with part7 body text.
summary: Mode 2b singleton verification of decider attention item asking whether §7.3 TLDR’s “within 8,500 km on a firmament” is consistent with the body text and the newly-aligned §7.4 TLDR. It is NOT consistent: §7.3 body says H(r) reaches 8,537 km at the pole (so “within 8,500 km” understates the actual maximum by 37 km and is technically wrong), §7.4 TLDR was just updated to “8,537 km at the pole”, and §7.3 body text was already updated by EXP-640 to use “8,537 km at the pole”. The §7.3 TLDR is now the lone outlier in Part 7 — every other Part 7 reference (§7.2 body, §7.3 body, §7.4 body, §7.4 TLDR) uses 8,537 km consistently. Proposing a single-string TLDR patch to harmonize.
kernel_of_truth: A rounded “8,500 km” is a defensible TLDR simplification for a flat-earth-level reader who does not care about 37 km of precision. Lay readers benefit from round numbers, and the body text carries the precise figure (this is the standard TLDR/detail discipline). But the rounding direction is wrong: “within 8,500 km” is a CEILING claim, and the actual maximum 8,537 km exceeds 8,500 km, so the TLDR is structurally inaccurate (a ceiling that is below the actual maximum). If the goal is round-number readability, “within 9,000 km” would at least be technically correct. The harmonization to 8,537 km matches §7.4’s newly-set convention and removes the inconsistency.

counter_argument: A defender could argue (a) TLDRs should use round numbers for readability, so 8,500 km is fine as a layman-facing approximation; (b) the TLDR rule (per CLAUDE.md Progressive Disclosure) is “fix factual errors, don’t split hairs on nuance,” and 37 km out of 8,500 is well within rounding noise that a flat-earth-level reader would ignore. The counter-counter: 8,500 km is a CEILING in this TLDR (“within 8,500”), not a typical value, so the rounding direction matters; understating a ceiling makes the claim technically wrong rather than approximately right. And the §7.4 TLDR was just updated by the decider to be precise, so harmonizing §7.3 to match is the consistency-cheap call.
